hints: Count the carbons carefully, you start with 3 carbons in 1-iodopropane but finish with 4 carbons in butanoic acid.
Remember which nucleophile can add an extra carbon to a halogenoalkane by forming a nitrile, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{CN}$.
Think what happens when that nitrile intermediate is heated with aqueous acid in stage two to give the carboxylic acid.
walkthrough:
**Spot the chain extension**

Well done for noticing the formulas first. You go from $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{I}$ to $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{CO}_2\text{H}$.

That is 3 carbons to 4 carbons, so stage one must add one carbon atom.

**Recall the cyanide route**

The classic way to add one carbon is nucleophilic substitution with cyanide ion, $\text{CN}^-$, to make a nitrile.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{I} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + \text{I}^-$$
This needs ethanolic potassium cyanide, heated under reflux.

**Check stage two completes the story**

In stage two, the nitrile (butanenitrile) is hydrolysed by heating with aqueous acid to give butanoic acid.

$$\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{CN} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{CO}_2\text{H} + \text{NH}_4^+$$
So the first reagent must be the one that makes the nitrile.

options.A: Aqueous sodium hydroxide gives nucleophilic substitution to an alcohol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. This keeps 3 carbons and cannot be hydrolysed to a 4-carbon acid.
options.B: Ethanolic ammonia gives nucleophilic substitution to a primary amine, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$. This also keeps 3 carbons and does not lead to a carboxylic acid.
options.C: Ethanolic potassium cyanide provides $\text{CN}^-$ for substitution to form butanenitrile, $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{CN}$. This adds the needed fourth carbon, and acid hydrolysis of the nitrile then gives butanoic acid.
options.D: Ethanolic sodium hydroxide causes elimination of $\text{HI}$ to form the alkene propene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$. This is the wrong reaction type and does not extend the chain.
